name: Listener crossword No 4,016: Motion
preamble: In 27 clues, motion has occurred. One letter has somehow moved to the beginning or end of the word in which it is found, and must be returned to its correct place before solving. In clue order, these letters give a thematic phrase describing the motion that must be applied to ten answers before entry into the grid. On entering 5dn, the result of the motion is inconclusive. The phrase at 19ac resolves the issue, as well as describing the final outcome. The Chambers Dictionary (2008) is the primary reference

clue.text: Antes pay nothing out without a cover

indicators.note: to be without something is to lack it, so a letter is taken away from the word before

blocks.note: printed with its A moved to the front; restored it is nates, the buttocks, for which can is slang
zero, written as the letter O
taken as written
taken as written; this letter is the one removed

explanation.surface: Gamblers putting nothing into the pot, with no protection over their heads.
explanation.walkthrough: The moved letter is the A in 'Antes', which belongs inside as nates. CANOPY contains NO, and the preamble's NOES TO THE LEFT sends NO to the front, so the grid gets NOCAPY.
explanation.definitionFit: A canopy is an overhead covering, such as fabric stretched above a bed or throne.

clue.text: Mourn decapitated bird

indicators.note: losing the head means the first letter is cut off

blocks.note: to mourn a loss is to regret it

explanation.surface: A grim image of grieving over a bird that has had its head cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decapitated' seems to describe the bird, but it acts on the verb for mourning. This clue has no moved letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a white heron, a wading water bird with long plumes.

clue.text: Sailor’s in the same place for a month

blocks.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
ib. is short for ibidem, Latin for in the same place, used in footnotes

explanation.surface: A seaman stays put in one spot for a whole month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sailor’s' reads as 'the sailor is'. The clue has no moved letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Abib is the old name for the first month of the Hebrew calendar, later called Nisan.

clue.text: Provinces see institute beset small Yarm branch

blocks.note: v. stands for vide, Latin for see
I is the abbreviation for institute
to lay for someone is to lie in wait and beset them
printed with its Y moved to the front; restored it is army, and ETS is short for the army's Educational and Training Services branch

explanation.surface: A note on regional government directing readers to an institute in the market town of Yarm.
explanation.walkthrough: Yarm is a real town in North Yorkshire, which hides the moved letter Y from army. VILAYETS contains AYE, which AYES TO THE RIGHT sends to the end: VILTSAYE.
explanation.definitionFit: A vilayet was an administrative province of the Ottoman Empire, so the plural means provinces.

clue.text: Fine gentleman a penny for having short hair

blocks.note: d. is the old abbreviation for a penny, from the Latin denarius
to be on a proposal is to be for it
not, or nott, is an old word for close-cropped or shorn

explanation.surface: A dandy pays a penny to get his hair cropped short.
explanation.walkthrough: No letter has moved in this clue. DONNOT contains NO, sent to the front under NOES TO THE LEFT, so the grid gets NODONT.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers records donnot as a rare, mainly Scots word for an idle showy fellow, which the setter glosses ironically as a dandified gent.

clue.text: Longing for chaos, ran away - backwards!

indicators.note: going backwards means running the other way, so these letters are taken in opposite order
something sent away is gone, so its letters are taken out of the longer word

blocks.note: anarchy is political chaos and lawlessness
taken as written; it is removed in reverse

explanation.surface: Someone craving disorder bolts the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chaos' tempts a solver to scramble letters, but it is a synonym, and 'backwards' applies to what is removed, not to the answer. This clue has no moved letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers allows achy for aching, and to ache for something is to long for it, so the adjective means longing.

clue.text: Crawled and decamped smuggling ether

indicators.note: a smuggler hides goods inside something, so one word is carried within another

blocks.note: to slide away is to slip off quietly, decamping
printed with an E moved to the front; restored it is there, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone crept away and fled with a bottle of anaesthetic hidden on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ether' looks like the chemical, but it is there with its last E moved to the front, the third letter of the thematic phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To slither is to move along by sliding, the way a snake or a person on their belly crawls.

clue.text: See preamble

blocks.note: the surface reading: a pointer to the instructions above the grid
the setter's reading: the phrase announcing a vote's result, which settles the tie left at the division lobby entry

explanation.walkthrough: After the motion, five AYEs sit right and five NOs left of the vertical entry; one more NO in this row breaks the tie. It is the Speaker's call after a vote in the House of Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the formal declaration in Parliament that the votes against a motion outnumber those for it.

clue.text: Angles covered in no-win situation?

indicators.note: anything covered in a layer is wrapped inside it, so the letters sit within the phrase

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of the second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A wry question about which angles you can take in a situation you cannot win.
explanation.walkthrough: This clue has no moved letter. Angles here are approaches, as in an in with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: An in is a way of gaining access or influence, an angle into a situation, so the plural fits.

clue.text: The rains troubled skell

indicators.note: something troubled is disturbed and thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Bad weather worries a skell, a homeless down-and-out in American slang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skell' is kells with its S moved to the front. A kell is an old word for a hairnet or a woman's caul.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives kell as a dialect word for a net cap worn over the hair, so kells are these nets.

clue.text: Townsman turned around “bust” drama for trade union

indicators.note: turning something around faces it the opposite way, so the letters run backwards
one thing given for another is exchanged for it, so a pair of letters is swapped out

blocks.note: printed with its T moved to the end; restored it is buts, objections, taken as written
No, or Noh, is the classical Japanese masked drama
TU is the standard abbreviation for trade union

explanation.walkthrough: '“bust”' is buts with its T moved to the end. In old Cambridge slang a snob was a townsman, as opposed to a gownsman of the university. The answer holds NO, moved left for the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Cambridge University slang called any non-member of the university living in the town by this word.

clue.text: Philosopher, 32, on wing ...

indicators.note: printed with its O moved to the front; restored it is no, and having no part means it is left out

blocks.note: the answer to 32 across, a layer of the upper atmosphere
an el, or ell, is a wing built at right angles to a house

explanation.surface: A thinker, borrowing another entry, takes flight and the sentence trails into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on wing' is no wing with the O moved to the front. A. J. Ayer was the British logical positivist philosopher. AYER sends AYE right in the grid: RAYE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Alfred Jules Ayer was a twentieth-century British thinker, author of Language, Truth and Logic.

clue.text: ... one might use these to glide about city openings

definitions.text: one might use these to glide

blocks.note: c. is short for circa, about
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
rents are tears or gaps, openings in fabric

explanation.surface: Continuing from the philosopher: he might use these to glide around a city's openings.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to the previous clue's philosopher, but the clue stands on its own. Gliders and birds ride rising air currents. No letter has moved here.
explanation.definitionFit: A glider or soaring bird rides flows of rising air, so these flows are what one uses to stay aloft.

clue.text: Call to back minuet up front

indicators.note: what is up front comes first, so only the opening letter is kept
to go back is to go the other way, so the short word is turned round

blocks.note: printed with its T moved to the end; restored it is minute, whose first letter is kept
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dancing master calls for the minuet to be repeated from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minuet' is minute with its T moved to the end. A mot is a note on a hunting horn, and in Chambers a call.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives mot as a note sounded on a bugle or hunting horn, a call to the hunt.

clue.text: Softly beginning to oink after pig’s heart is found in basin

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept
the heart of a word is its centre, so only the middle letter is kept
to be found in something is to sit inside it
coming after means placed later, so this piece follows the rest

blocks.note: a pan is a shallow basin
the middle letter of the three
its opening letter

explanation.walkthrough: No letter has moved in this clue. PIANO contains NO, which goes to the front: NOPIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Piano is the Italian musical direction to play softly, the opposite of forte.

clue.text: Reel about clutching an unknown region high above the heart

indicators.note: to be about is to be turned round and stirred, so the letters are rearranged
clutching something holds it tight inside the hands

blocks.note: taken as written
the indefinite article as a single letter
y is one of the algebraic unknowns

explanation.surface: Feeling giddy at grasping something unknown far above one's chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' is earth with its H moved to the front, so the region is high above the earth. E-LAYER contains AYE, which goes to the right end: ELRAYE.
explanation.definitionFit: The E-layer is a band of the ionosphere about a hundred kilometres up, which reflects radio waves.

clue.text: Princess starts to sense vile, nasty demands of wedding, so withdraws dowry

indicators.note: the start of each word is its first letter, so only those are kept

blocks.note: Di, as in Diana, Princess of Wales

blocks.clueFragment: sense vile, nasty demands of wedding, so
blocks.note: the initials, reading the misprinted vile as evil, its E moved to the end

explanation.surface: A princess senses foul wedding demands and takes back the dowry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vile' is evil with its E moved to the end, so its initial counts as E. 'so' supplies both the last initial and the sense of consequence.
explanation.definitionFit: To disendow is to strip something of its endowment; a dowry is an endowment, so withdrawing one fits.

clue.text: Pincer movement primarily in Ireland, driving out English

to be in something is to sit inside it

blocks.note: Éire is the Irish name for Ireland
E is the abbreviation for English; it is removed
its first letter

explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a Muslim ruler or prince, especially in the Middle East.

clue.text: French town’s imam buys sex with amateur for two dollars

indicators.note: one thing given for another replaces it in the letters
printed with its I moved to the front; restored it is maim, and maimed letters are mangled out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
A is the abbreviation for amateur
the dollar sign looks like an S, so two dollars give two

explanation.walkthrough: 'imam' is maim, the anagram signal, with its I moved to the front. The A replaces the two S's before the letters are mixed. BAYEUX holds AYE, sent right: BUXAYE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bayeux is a town in Normandy, home of the famous tapestry of the Norman Conquest.

clue.text: One consumed by Gore capsized boat in Mountie’s home?

indicators.note: a capsized vessel is overturned and thrown into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

taken as written
i' is a dialect shortening of in

explanation.surface: A politician swallows a man and a boat overturns near a Canadian policeman's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gore' looks like Al Gore, but it is ogre with the G moved. Mounties are the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, so a Canadian province can be called a Mountie's home; the question mark flags the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Manitoba is a prairie province of Canada, policed by the Royal Canadian Mounted Police.

clue.text: Soil has initially dropped from each plough

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is used
dropping something from a group leaves it out

blocks.note: printed with its H moved to the front; restored it is ash, whose first letter is used
ea. is the abbreviation for each
an ard is a primitive plough that scratches the soil

explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is ash with its H moved to the front. EA and ARD join with two A's together, and one of them is the A that drops out.
explanation.definitionFit: Eard is a Scots and old form of earth, so it means soil or ground.

clue.text: Crowd sent back teas for Sprite

blocks.note: mong is a dialect word for a crowd or mixture

explanation.definitionFit: A gnome is a goblin-like spirit of folklore, one kind of sprite or elf.

clue.text: Topless doctor with escort backing people getting the necessary

indicators.note: with no top, the word loses its first letter
to back is to go in reverse, so these letters run the other way

blocks.note: to doctor an animal is to neuter it, and to spay a female
to see someone home is to escort them

explanation.definitionFit: Payees are those to whom money is paid, and the necessary is informal for cash.

clue.text: Grandmother’s affectionate “amen” - her daughter’s leaving tomorrow

indicators.note: someone leaving goes away, so those letters are taken out

blocks.note: mañana is Spanish for tomorrow
a grandmother's daughter is a mother, MA

explanation.walkthrough: 'amen' is name with its N moved to the end, so the definition is a grandmother's affectionate name. Her daughter is the mother of the family, MA.

clue.text: Stop man ensnared by rising game

bo is an American word for a pal or man

explanation.surface: An order for a man to stop when caught by a rising hunted animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' is an organ stop, not a halt. No letter has moved in this clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboe is an organ stop with a reedy tone imitating the woodwind instrument.

clue.text: Swarm on all sides - run away, swallowing bee

swallowing takes something inside

blocks.note: around means surrounding on every side
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
the letter B is pronounced bee

clue.text: Bridge opens, bypassing the centre of Leeds

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, so only that letter is used
bypassing something leaves it out of the route

blocks.note: printed with its O moved to the front; restored it is peons, labourers
the middle letter of the five

explanation.walkthrough: 'opens' is peons, Latin American labourers, with the O moved to the front. PONS holds neither AYE nor NO, so it is entered unchanged.

clue.text: See preamble

blocks.note: the surface reading: a pointer to the instructions above the grid
the setter's reading: the place where members go to record a vote, the theme of the motion

explanation.walkthrough: Members of the House of Commons vote by walking through one of two corridors, ayes one way and noes the other. In the grid this entry is the dividing line the moved AYEs and NOs sit either side of.

clue.text: Heads of cunning elvers are shifting threat, like a net?

an are is a unit of area, A
taken as written

clue.text: After climax of rave, the slogan spoken again and again is “acid”

indicators.note: the climax comes at the end, so only the last letter is kept

blocks.note: its final letter

a chant is a slogan repeated over and over

clue.text: Take away hollow pines

blocks.note: R is short for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions
its first and last letters

explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives ray as one of the stiff spines or rods that support a fish's fin.

clue.text: Wait on the return of rapt daughter

explanation.walkthrough: 'rapt' is trap with its T moved to the end. No AYE or NO in TEND, so it is entered as it stands.

clue.text: Assembly’s spirited away vacuous Tory

something taken away is removed

blocks.note: feisty means spirited and lively
its first and last letters

explanation.walkthrough: A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party. No letter has moved here.

clue.text: Muddles master with drinks

sups are sips or small drinks

explanation.walkthrough: 'Muddles' could be a verb, but it is the plural noun. No letter has moved in this clue.

blocks.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis

blocks.note: to ret is to rot or soak flax
taken as written

has shortens to 's

clue.text: Apt pages set down with no Latin

to drop something is to set it down

explanation.walkthrough: 'Apt' is tap with its T moved to the end, and to tap a phone is to listen in secretly.

clue.text: Sooth European move for Nijinsky, perhaps

clue.text: Cheese barrel split, shedding volume

blocks.note: b. is short for barrel
to rive is to split or tear apart
V is the abbreviation for volume

clue.text: Though propping up company, it’s a shock arrangement

blocks.note: Co. is short for company
if, as in 'even if', means though
